'''Watarai Kunimi Shrine''' (度会国御神社, *Watarai Kunimi Jinja*) is an [[auxiliary shrine]] (*sessha*) of [[Ise Grand Shrine]] ({{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, *Gekū*). It is located within the precincts of the Gekū, along a small path beside the North Gate.<ref name="i">{{ill|ITV|en|ITV|qid=Q246568|lt=ITV}} "[http://www.yoitokose.jp/ise/encyclopedia/w0001.php Watarai Kunimi Shrine | Ise Grand Shrine Encyclopedia | Ise-Shima Travel Yoitokose]" (Accessed April 3, 2011)</ref>

== Overview ==

Located about 900 meters southwest of {{ill|Iseshi Station|en|Iseshi Station|qid=Q6079748|lt=Ise Station}}<ref name="sk0">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 320</ref>, {{ill|Watarai Kunimi Shrine|ja|度会国御神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Watarai Kokumika Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11486118}} sits within the precincts of the {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|外宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gekū (Ise Grand Shrine)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 豊受大神宮|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11633343}} in {{ill|Toyokawachō|ja|豊川町 (伊勢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokawa-chō, Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17223204}}, {{ill|Ise, Mie|en|Ise, Mie|qid=Q328067|lt=Ise, Mie}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}. Among the auxiliary shrines of the Gekū, it Ranks third after {{ill|Kusanagi Shrine (Ise)|ja|草奈伎神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusanaki Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17228323}} and {{ill|Kusanagi Shrine (Ise)|ja|大間国生神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmakuni Musubi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 草奈伎神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17228323}}.

The enshrined deity is {{ill|Hikokunimigaki Takeyotsuka no Mikoto|ja|彦國見賀岐建與束命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikokunimigaki Takeyotsuka no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}<ref>Ujiyamada City Office (1929): p. 12</ref> (ひこくにみがきたけよつかのみこと<ref name="ic">Ise Bunkasha (2008): p. 37</ref>), regarded as the {{ill|Kunitsukami|ja|国魂神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kunitsukami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 国魂}} (guardian deity of the land) of Ise Province. He is said to be the son of {{ill|Amihiwake no Mikoto|ja|天日別命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Hiwake no Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q106107046}}, the ancestral deity of the {{ill|Ise no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|伊勢国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuni no Miyatsuko of Ise|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise no Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}}, who historically governed northern Ise. His mother is unknown.

The shrine building follows the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|qid=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri}} architectural style, with a wooden plank roof, enclosed by a sacred fence ({{ill|Sacred fences|en|Tamagaki|qid=Q3078312|lt=Tamagaki}})<ref name="sk2">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 322</ref>. There is no offering box. Further beyond Watarai Kokumika Shrine lies the {{ill|Ōtsu Shrine (Ise)|ja|大津神社 (伊勢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtsu Shrine (Ise)|qq=}}, another auxiliary shrine of the Gekū.

== History ==

Originally known as the Shrine of Watarai no Kunitsumikami (度会国都御神の社), the name has been standardized as Watarai Kokumika Shrine following its listing in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}<ref>Sakurai (1998): p. 86</ref>.

The exact date of its founding is unknown<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 321</ref>, but it is believed to predate the establishment of the Gekū during the 22nd year of Emperor Yūryaku’s reign<ref name="i"/>. Regarding the shrine, {{ill|Katsunoshin Sakurai|ja|櫻井勝之進|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakurai Katsunosuke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11544758}} wrote:

{{Quotation|When a society is unified under a central authority and integrated into the nation's structure, the deities worshipped there are also incorporated as gods related to the supreme deity of the nation, either through divine lineage or divine association, as depicted in myths regarding the relationship between ancient Izumo and the central government.
|Sakurai Katsunosuke, *Ise Jingū*, p. 35}}

This suggests that when the influential {{ill|Watarai clan|ja|度会氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Watarai clan|qq=}} of {{ill|Q11588058|ja|磯部 (部民)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isobe|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 磯部|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11588058}} was entrusted with the worship of {{ill|Toyouke-hime|ja|豊受大御神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-Ōmikami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to トヨウケビメ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2983724}}<ref>Sakurai (1998): p. 35</ref>, the deities they had been venerating were integrated into Ise Jingū’s pantheon.

The shrine was initially located in {{ill|Yamada|ja|山田 (伊勢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada, Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11470062}} Maeda Village. According to *Ninomiya Kansha Enkaku Kō*, the villagers of Maeno served Watarai Kokumika Shrine as their {{ill|Ubusunagami|en|Ubusunagami|qid=Q1392097|lt=Ubusunagami}}<ref name="sk0"/>. In the medieval period, the establishment of {{ill|Segi-dera Temple|ja|世義寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Segi-ji Temple|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11362520}} within the precincts temporarily disrupted the shrine’s rituals. However, during the Kanbun era (1661–1672), Segi-ji was relocated, and the shrine's deity was also moved to the same site<ref name="sk0"/>.

Before its relocation, Segi-ji Temple was situated near present-day {{ill|Q11391248|ja|八日市場町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yōkaichiba-chō, Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11391248}}, close to the Jingū Yamada Workshop<ref name="sk0"/>. Eventually, the shrine was separated from the temple and moved to its current location, which had served as its place of worship<ref name="sk0"/>.

The shrine building was reconstructed in December 1956 (Shōwa 31) and underwent major renovations on April 10, 1980 (Shōwa 55)<ref name="sk2"/>.

Fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|qid=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} pottery have been found at the shrine site<ref>Ise City (2011): p. 364</ref>, with most of the discovered ceramics identified as Sue pottery<ref>Ise City (2011): p. 370</ref>.

== Rituals ==

Major festivals include the {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinamisai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} with grand offerings ({{ill|Ōmikesai|ja|大御饌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmikesai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) and presentations ({{ill|Hōhei|ja|奉幣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hōhei|qq=}}) on June 19 and December 19; the {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}} on October 19; and the {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niinamesai}} on November 25<ref name="sk2"/>.

Other rituals, such as:
* {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}} (January 1)
* {{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Genshi-sai|qq=}} (January 3)
* National Foundation Day Festival (February 11)
* {{ill|Kinensai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinensai}} (February 19)
* {{ill|Kazahi-no-Misai|ja|風日祈祭|2=ja|3=風日祈祭|qid=Q135524493|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaze-no-hi-no-matsuri|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135524493}} (May 14 & August 4)
* {{ill|The Emperor's Birthday|ja|天長祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenchō-sai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天皇誕生日|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q72318}} (December 23)

These are conducted via remote worship at the Gojō-den Hall of the Gekū<ref name="sk2"/>.

== Access ==

;To Gekū Front
* 5-minute walk from JR {{ill|Sangū Line|en|Sangū Line|qid=Q872023|lt=Sangū Line}} or {{ill|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|en|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|qid=Q900630|lt=Kintetsu Yamada Line}} Ise City Station (south exit).
* 5-minute walk from Mie Kōtsū, Sankō Ise-Shima Kōtsū, or {{ill|Q11379021|ja|おかげバス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okage Bus|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 伊勢市コミュニティバス|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11379021}} "Ise City Station" bus stop.
* Immediate access from Mie Kōtsū's "Gekū-mae" bus stop.
* About 5 minutes from {{ill|Ise-nishi itnerchange|ja|伊勢西インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise-Nishi Interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10884865}} on the {{ill|Ise Expressway|en|Ise Expressway|qid=Q6079578|lt=Ise Expressway}}, heading north via Mie Prefectural Route 32 (Mokimoto Road), with a free parking lot for 434 vehicles near the North Gate<ref>Mie Prefecture Tourism Federation "[http://www.kankomie.or.jp/sagasu12_barrier/barifuri/leisure/area_ise/01-jingu.html Mie Barrier-Free Leisure Guide]" (Accessed April 11, 2011)</ref>.

;Within the Gekū Precinct
* Proceed west along the path in front of the Gokura to reach the shrine<ref>Ise Bunkasha (2008): p. 36</ref>.
